As the monarch lives outside of New Zealand, the governor-general personally represents the monarch and performs most of his or her domestic duties in their absence, in accordance with Letters Patent 1983.

✓ Monarchy of New Zealand.question: In 1953, for her coronation, _____ was given a kiwi feather korowai cloak, which she wore when attending a pōwhiri, or Māori welcoming ceremony, also speaking partly in Māori
✓ Monarchy of New Zealand.fact: In the Māori language, Queen Elizabeth II is sometimes called te kōtuku-rerenga-tahi, meaning "the white heron of a single flight"; in Māori proverb, the rare white heron is a significant bird seen only once in a lifetime. In 1953, for her coronation, Elizabeth was given a kiwi feather korowai cloak, which she wore when attending a pōwhiri, or Māori welcoming ceremony, also speaking partly in Māori.

✓ Monarchy of New Zealand.fact: On 28 October 1835, Busby oversaw a hui held at Waitangi, at which a flag was selected for New Zealand and a declaration of independence written by Busby was signed by 36 Māori chiefs. The Treaty of Waitangi was signed in 1840 by representatives of the British Crown and over 500 Māori chiefs, It is considered to be a founding document of government.
